summary_paragraph: A woman with a complex medical history including end-stage renal disease, pancreatic transplant, mechanical mitral valve, and heart failure was admitted for left leg cellulitis following a bug bite at her dialysis center. She presented with fever, chills, nausea, and worsening leg pain. She had been on reduced-dose warfarin, leading to an elevated INR of 4 on admission. She was treated with intravenous vancomycin after initial broad-spectrum antibiotics at an outside hospital. Her infection improved, INR normalized, and warfarin was safely restarted. She received one session of hemodialysis during admission and was transitioned back to her baseline medications, including metoprolol, which had been held. She was discharged home with a plan to complete a 10-day course of vancomycin via dialysis, monitor INR, and follow up with her care teams.
problems: Cellulitis and abscess of leg, except foot
Anticoagulants causing adverse effects in therapeutic use
Heart valve replaced by other means
